title: Bun.build(): Zig AST Parser & Multi-Threaded Chunk Splitting

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In Node.js, bundling a website means a JavaScript program slowly reads every file and glues them together. In Bun, a high-speed machine written in Zig reads your code, strips TypeScript, splits it into small fast chunks, and builds the entire application in a fraction of a second.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `Bun.build()` is Bun's built-in, native JavaScript/TypeScript bundler. You run it from the CLI with `bun build ./src/index.ts --outdir ./dist` or via JavaScript: `await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./src/index.ts'], outdir: './dist', minify: true, splitting: true })`. It replaces Webpack, Rollup, and esbuild with zero npm dependencies and natively supports TypeScript, JSX, and custom plugins.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `Bun.build` uses a custom parallel AST parser and code generator written in Zig. It constructs an in-memory module graph, resolves imports using Bun's native module resolver, performs dead-code elimination (tree-shaking), and handles multi-threaded code-splitting into ES module chunks. The plugin API (`bun:plugins`) allows intercepting import resolutions (`onResolve`) and asset loading (`onLoad`) with minimal overhead.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: The Zig compiler pipeline parses source files into a custom binary AST using SIMD scanners. Imports are resolved concurrently across native threads. The bundler builds an internal topological sort of dependencies, eliminates unused exports via scope-reachability analysis, allocates shared chunks for common dependencies, and generates output `.js` bundles using a parallel printer that writes directly to disk via native system calls.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you write a custom loader plugin for Bun.build to import non-standard files (like `.yaml` or `.svg`)?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of Bun's plugin lifecycle API.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Create a plugin object with a `setup(build)` function. Use `build.onLoad({ filter: /\.yaml$/ }, async (args) => { const text = await Bun.file(args.path).text(); return { exports: parseYaml(text), loader: 'object' }; })`. Register the plugin in `Bun.build({ plugins: [myYamlPlugin] })`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Plugins in `Bun.build` execute asynchronously, but excessive JavaScript plugin calls can reduce raw Zig bundler throughput.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `Bun.build` bundle applications targeting Node.js as well as the browser?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of compilation targets in `Bun.build`.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. Set `target: 'node'` or `target: 'browser'` or `target: 'bun'`. Setting `target: 'node'` ensures that built-in Node modules (`node:fs`, `node:path`) are treated as external imports rather than bundled into the output.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: The default target is `'browser'`; forgetting to set `target: 'node'` when bundling server tools will cause runtime errors if Node built-ins are bundled unexpectedly.
